evals.prompt: Map an instructor-led programming course for children with no computer experience. Start from what a computer is and reach a first web page. List the entire table of contents and proposed projects, but do not write lessons or media yet.
evals.expected_output: Creates only a valid course-plan.json and synchronized README; hierarchy is sections > chapters > lessons > concepts; computer basics precede code; each chapter has a small project; at least three small projects precede the first section project.

evals.prompt: Using an existing course map, move the lesson on file extensions after the operating-system lesson. Keep its ID and existing notes path. Check prerequisites and update the table of contents only where needed.
evals.expected_output: Updates map order and generated table of contents without regenerating lessons or media; preserves stable IDs and teacher edits; validates prerequisite order and artifact paths.

evals.prompt: Write only the lesson on file extensions for an absolute beginner. Use my story about a child sorting school files. Include a practical file task but no exercise bank.
evals.expected_output: Creates one lesson with example first, What/Why/Where/When/How, a visual explanation plan, demonstration, and learner check; does not create unrelated lessons or an exercise bank.

evals.prompt: Create fifteen optional practice exercises and a publishable online assignment package for the file extensions lesson. Keep answers separate from learner materials.
evals.expected_output: Produces requested exercises and an assignment with instructions, submission requirements, starter material if needed, rubric, and separate teacher guidance; does not build hosting or student accounts.

evals.prompt: Create the Slidev deck for the hardware lesson. Use images in the course folder first; if none fits, find a reusable image with credit, then generate or draw one. Export a slide handout PDF only if requested later.
evals.expected_output: Creates one editable, concept-mapped Slidev deck and storyboard; records source, usage terms, alt text, and caption for visuals; does not export PDF or video.

evals.prompt: Turn the hardware lesson deck and my recorded teacher video plus transcript into a Remotion lesson video. Place me beside the diagram for the demonstration, add captions, and prepare a CapCut Desktop editing package.
evals.expected_output: Loads relevant video skills, writes shared and per-video style.md including an effects bible, aligns scenes and captions to footage, creates editable Remotion source and MP4 when rendering works, and packages separate CapCut media with a timecoded editing guide.

evals.prompt: Create a beginner lesson about the water cycle for adult learners, then make just its notes as a PDF and an online page source. No programming stack, fixed exercise count, slide deck, or video is needed.
evals.expected_output: Handles a nontechnical subject, creates only the lesson and requested notes outputs, uses appropriate factual sources, and does not impose programming requirements or unrelated assets.

evals.prompt: Expand the written course only: create a chapter overview, one lesson, a weekly schedule, and an alphabetical index. Use the existing course map and preserve its project ideas. No slides or video are requested.
evals.expected_output: Produces the selected written assets with navigation and stable IDs, uses the preserved text-course guidance where helpful, and creates no media outputs.

evals.prompt: Use Kokoro to narrate only this supplied lesson script. Save editable text and a WAV; do not create slides, captions, or video.
evals.expected_output: Uses the local Kokoro workflow to create and verify a WAV, records narrationText and narrationAudio with their dependency, and does not create unrelated outputs.

evals.prompt: For the existing file extensions lesson, make a Slidev deck, Kokoro narration, and Remotion video based on the deck. Leave the written notes alone, and record what depends on what so later edits can be refreshed selectively.
evals.expected_output: Creates only the requested deck, narration, and video artifacts; aligns them by stable concept and beat IDs; writes a per-video style.md; records actual artifactSources and staleArtifacts in the course map.

evals.prompt: I sell beginner coding skills. Write five opening hooks and one short enrollment post for parents whose children have never used a computer. Use the existing course map; there is a sample lesson but no verified job promise, certificate, or limited-time offer. Do not write lessons or make a video.
evals.expected_output: Uses specific beginner learner problems and real sample-lesson or project proof, gives five distinct honest hooks and one clear next step, avoids invented guarantees or urgency, and creates only marketing copy.

evals.prompt: Make a Slidev lesson about browsers using suitable icons already inside the course-creator assets folder. Keep the deck portable, include alt text and source details, and do not make a video.
evals.expected_output: Inspects matching bundled SVGs, copies selected useful icons into the course, uses them in a concept-mapped deck, records provenance and any unresolved public reuse terms, and creates no video.

evals.prompt: Launch my coding course as a product. I supplied screenshots of the course page, one sample lesson, and a learner project, plus a URL with product details. Create a Remotion motion ad that shows the real screens. Do not invent enrollment claims or use TTS unless I ask.
evals.expected_output: Reads the supplied product source and screenshots, writes a claim-grounded brief, storyboard, and per-video style.md, creates editable Remotion source and MP4 when rendering works, records course-level artifact dependencies, and keeps unshown interactions out of the demo.

evals.prompt: Only the course-creator parent skill is installed. Create the file extensions lesson, its Slidev deck using a bundled icon, and a Kokoro WAV for my supplied narration script. Do not create a video.
evals.expected_output: Routes to the bundled text, slides, assets, and TTS subskills without relying on separately installed sibling skills; creates only the requested outputs and records their actual dependencies.
